svg.font-family: 'Avenir Next', Avenir, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: The gain lands where the experience isn't
svg.desc: In a study of 5,172 customer support agents, AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour by 15 percent on average, and by 30 percent among less-skilled and less-experienced workers. The advantage accrued first to the people with the least experience, appearing to move the patterns used by the strongest workers down the experience curve.
svg.text: What the tool does to a beginner
Issues resolved per hour with AI assistance, among 5,172 customer-support agents.
Twice the average gain. The tool appeared to move the
strongest workers' patterns down the experience curve.
The advantage accrued first to the people with the least experience.
Customer support is not occupational retraining — but it reveals the mechanism. Source: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond,
“Generative AI at Work,” Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2025.
